'''Anne Marie Wilkinson''' (born 1968) is an American mathematician and [[professor]] of [[mathematics]] at the [[University of Chicago]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Amie Wilkinson {{!}} Department of Mathematics {{!}} The University of Chicago|url=https://mathematics.uchicago.edu/people/profile/amie-wilkinson/|access-date=2021-10-26|website=mathematics.uchicago.edu}}</ref> Her research topics include smooth [[dynamical system]]s, [[ergodic theory]], [[chaos theory]], and [[Semisimple Lie algebra|semisimple]] [[Lie group]]s.<ref name=":0" /> Wilkinson, in collaboration with Christian Bonatti and Sylvain Crovisier,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Bonatti|first1=Christian|last2=Crovisier|first2=Sylvain|last3=Wilkinson|first3=Amie|year=2008|title=''C''<sup>1</sup>-generic conservative diffeomorphisms have trivial centralizers|journal=Journal of Modern Dynamics|volume=2|pages=359–373|doi=10.3934/jmd.2008.2.359|doi-access=free|arxiv=0710.3989}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Bonatti|first1=Christian|last2=Crovisier|first2=Sylvain|last3=Wilkinson|first3=Amie|year=2009|title=The ''C''<sup>1</sup>-generic diffeomorphism has trivial centralizer|journal=Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS|volume=109|pages=185–244|arxiv=0804.1416|doi=10.1007/s10240-009-0021-z|s2cid=16212782}}</ref> partially resolved the twelfth problem on [[Smale's problems|Stephen Smale's list of mathematical problems for the 21st Century]].<ref>{{cite journal|last=Smale|first=Steve|year=1998|title=Mathematical Problems for the Next Century|journal=Mathematical Intelligencer|volume=20|pages=7–15|citeseerx=10.1.1.35.4101|doi=10.1007/bf03025291|number=2|s2cid=1331144}}</ref>

Wilkinson was named a [[fellow]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]] (AMS) in 2014.<ref name=":1">{{cite magazine|author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.-->|date=April 2014|title=2014 Class of the Fellows of the AMS|url=https://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/fellows2014.pdf|magazine=Notices of the AMS|publisher=AMS|volume=61|pages=420–421|access-date=2016-03-21|number=4}}</ref> She was elected to the [[Academia Europaea]]<ref>{{citation|title=Amie Wilkinson|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Wilkinson_Amie|work=Elected members 2019|publisher=Academia Europaea|access-date=2019-09-05}}</ref> in 2019 and the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2021.<ref name=":2">{{cite web|title=New Members Elected in 2021|url=https://www.amacad.org/new-members-2021|access-date=2021-04-22|publisher=American Academy of Arts and Sciences}}</ref> In 2020, she received the [[Levi L. Conant Prize]] of the AMS for her overview article on the modern theory of [[Lyapunov exponent]]s and their applications to diverse areas of dynamical systems and mathematical physics.<ref name="Levi L. Conant Prize 2020">[https://www.ams.org/tools/news?news_id=5588 Levi L. Conant Prize 2020]</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=News from the AMS|url=https://www.ams.org/tools/news?news_id=5588|access-date=2021-10-26|website=American Mathematical Society|language=en}}</ref>

==Biography==
Anne Marie Wilkinson was born to Ruth E. VanDemark and Leland Wilkinson.<ref name="marriage">{{cite news |title=Amie Wilkinson, Benson S. Farb |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1996/12/29/style/amie-wilkinson-benson-s-farb.html |work=[[New York Times]] |date=29 December 1996 |language=en |access-date=2021-12-14}}</ref>

She received a [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree in mathematics from [[Harvard University]] in 1989 and a [[PhD]] in Mathematics from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1995 under the direction of [[Charles C. Pugh]].<ref name="satterprize">{{cite magazine |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |title=2011 Satter Prize |url=https://www.ams.org/notices/201104/rtx110400601p.pdf |magazine=Notices of the AMS |volume=58 |number=4 |pages=601–602 |publisher=AMS |date=April 2011 |access-date=2016-03-21 }}</ref> She is currently a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Chicago]] and was previously a professor of mathematics at [[Northwestern University]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Janofsky |first=Adam |date=12 March 2013 |title=Q&A: Amie Wilkinson |url=https://chicagomaroon.com/16901/grey-city/qa-amie-wilkinson/ |work=[[The Chicago Maroon]] |location=Chicago |access-date=30 September 2023}}</ref>

==Work==
Wilkinson's work focuses on the geometric and statistical properties of [[diffeomorphism]]s and flows with a particular emphasis on stable [[ergodicity]] and partial [[hyperbolicity]].  In a series of papers with [[Christian Bonatti]] and [[Sylvain Crovisier]], Wilkinson studied centralizers of diffeomorphisms<ref>{{cite journal  | first1 = Christian | last1 = Bonatti  | first2 = Sylvain | last2 = Crovisier | first3 = Amie | last3 = Wilkinson | title = ''C''<sup>1</sup>-generic conservative diffeomorphisms have trivial centralizers |  journal =  Journal of Modern Dynamics | year = 2008 | volume = 2 | pages =  359–373 | doi=10.3934/jmd.2008.2.359| doi-access = free | arxiv = 0710.3989 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal  | first1 = Christian | last1 = Bonatti  | first2 = Sylvain | last2 = Crovisier | first3 = Amie | last3 = Wilkinson | title = The ''C''<sup>1</sup>-generic diffeomorphism has trivial centralizer | journal = Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS|volume = 109 | year = 2009 | pages = 185–244 | doi=10.1007/s10240-009-0021-z| arxiv = 0804.1416 | s2cid = 16212782 }}</ref> settling the [[smoothness|''C''<sup>1</sup>]] case of the twelfth problem on [[Smale's problems|Stephen Smale's list of mathematical problems for the 21st Century]].<ref>{{cite journal | first = Steve | last = Smale|title = Mathematical Problems for the Next Century|journal = Mathematical Intelligencer|year =1998|volume=20|number=2|pages=7–15|citeseerx = 10.1.1.35.4101|doi=10.1007/bf03025291| s2cid = 1331144}}</ref>

==Awards==
Wilkinson was the recipient of the 2011 [[Satter Prize in Mathematics]],<ref name="satterprize" /> in part for her work with [[Keith Burns (mathematician)|Keith Burns]] on stable ergodicity of partially hyperbolic systems.<ref>{{cite journal | first1 = Keith | last1 = Burns | first2 = Amie | last2 = Wilkinson | title = On the ergodicity of partially hyperbolic systems | journal = Annals of Mathematics | year =  2010 | volume = 171 | number = 1 | pages = 451–489 | doi=10.4007/annals.2010.171.451| doi-access = free | arxiv = math/0510234 }}</ref>

She gave an invited talk, "Dynamical Systems and Ordinary Differential Equations", in the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] 2010 in [[Hyderabad, India]].<ref>{{cite web|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers since 1897|url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByCongress.php|publisher=[[International Congress of Mathematicians]]|access-date=2013-08-15|archive-date=2017-11-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171108012153/http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByCongress.php|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2013 she became a [[fellow]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]], for "contributions to dynamical systems".<ref>{{cite magazine |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |title=2014 Class of the Fellows of the AMS |url=https://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/fellows2014.pdf |magazine=Notices of the AMS |volume=61 |number=4 |pages=420–421 |publisher=AMS |date=April 2014 |access-date=2016-03-21 }}</ref> In 2019 she was elected to the [[Academia Europaea]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Wilkinson_Amie|title=Amie Wilkinson|work=Elected members 2019|publisher=Academia Europaea|access-date=2019-09-05}}</ref> In 2020 she received the [[Levi L. Conant Prize]] of the AMS.<ref name="Levi L. Conant Prize 2020"/> She was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.amacad.org/new-members-2021|title=New Members Elected in 2021|publisher=American Academy of Arts and Sciences|access-date=2021-04-22}}</ref>

Wilkinson has been featured in articles in [[Quanta Magazine]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Hartnett|first=Kevin|date=2019-06-13|title=A Mathematician Whose Only Constant Is Change|url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/a-mathematician-whose-only-constant-is-change-20190613/|access-date=2021-10-26|website=Quanta Magazine|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Strogatz|first=Steven|date=2021-05-03|title=Amie Wilkinson Sees the Dynamic Chaos in Puff Pastry|url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/amie-wilkinson-sees-the-dynamic-chaos-in-puff-pastry-20210503/|access-date=2021-10-26|website=Quanta Magazine|language=en}}</ref> Wilkinson is a member of the Board of Advisers of [[Scientific American]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/pressroom/board-of-advisers/ |title=Board of Advisers |website=[[Scientific American]] |access-date=2022-04-06}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Wilkinson married [[Benson Farb]] on December 28, 1996. They are professors in the same department.<ref name="marriage"/>
